name: Redis: a MADV_FREE page rewritten before fork() must remain private-dirty in the child (arm64 pte_wrprotect bug probe)
required_postconditions: the 3-page mapping is not merged with an adjacent VMA - Redis enforces this by setting RO|RW|RO protections across the three pages (syscheck.c:225-227)
after madvise(MADV_FREE) and a subsequent write, the page is re-owned by the process

after fork(), /proc/self/smaps in the CHILD must report a non-zero Shared_Dirty for that page; zero means the kernel dropped the dirty bit across pte_wrprotect() and the page can be silently reclaimed
the allocator's MADV_FREE-based purging is therefore safe to combine with fork-based persistence

failure_sink.description: the check returns -1 and syscheck reports "Your kernel has a bug that could lead to data corruption during background save. Please upgrade to the latest stable kernel." (syscheck.c:296). Reached from `redis-server --check-system`, which exits non-zero (server.c:8177). The condition it detects is silent data corruption in the RDB written by the background save.

source_locations.symbol: p = mmap(NULL, map_size, PROT_READ, MAP_ANONYMOUS | MAP_PRIVATE, -1, 0); with map_size = 3 * page_size
child: ret = smapsGetSharedDirty((unsigned long) q); - 'A value of 0 means the kernel is affected by the bug.'
comment naming the fix: ' * titled: "arm64: pgtable: Ensure dirty bit is preserved across pte_wrprotect()"'

extraction_limitations: nothing in this document expresses what the check is actually about. There is no field for fork(), for copy-on-write, for MADV_FREE, for VMA merging, or for page-table dirty-bit preservation. The request below is only the mmap that sets the stage; the requirement lives entirely in required_postconditions as prose
the whole check is compiled only under #ifdef __arm64__ (syscheck.c:172, registered at syscheck.c:325); on the x86-64 campaign host this code does not exist

x_campaign.rationale: A 12KiB anonymous RW mapping with no address is unobjectionable to every rule in the analyzer, so I expect a bare SUPPORTED. The postconditions that carry the entire requirement are free text the engine never reads.
